newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wool prices ease at New Zealand sales.
newsitem.headline: Wool prices ease at New Zealand sales.

text.p: Wool prices generally eased at sales in Napier and Christchurch on Thursday, reflecting the continued appreciation of the New Zealand dollar, Wools of New Zealand said.
The provisional indicators moved as follows: strong down six cents to NZ$4.24, fine down three to $8.17, medium down five to $4.98 and the overall market indicator down three to $4.64.

The offering was 35,247 bales, 4,159 clean tonnes, of which 21 percent was passed in after failing to meet growers' price reserves. Crossbred fleece (39 percent), second shear (19 percent) and merino (16 percent) made up most of the offering.

Compared with the Christchurch sale on October 31, merino prices were mixed, with 18 micron best topmaking generally five to 7.5 percent dearer and 18 micron good topmaking par to five percent cheaper.
Halfbred fleece 24 and 25 micron was one to two percent dearer while 30 to 32 micron was one to two percent cheaper.

Crossbred fleece, second shear, bulky skirtings and second shear bellies and pieces were all cheaper. Principal interest came from Western Europe, China and local mills with support from Australia, the United States, Japan, India and Nepal. The next sale is at Napier on November 14.
